label: def:hecke-mass-element
title: Hecke mass element
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a (quantum observable universe) with Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) (Hecke algebra) and Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(R, q) \to k (Jones--Markov trace).

Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a vortex morphism with braid representative \beta \in B_n. The mass integrand (mass identity) is the composition

  \alpha_\varrho
  =
  (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ \Delta
  \circ \varrho
  \colon \mathbf{1} \to A,

which, via left multiplication in the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A, determines an endomorphism L_{\alpha_\varrho} \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A). Since all constituent maps (\Delta, \int_A, \varrho) are morphisms in \mathbf{C}, the fibre-functor image \tau(L_{\alpha_\varrho}) is an \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-equivariant endomorphism of V^{\otimes n}. By quantum Schur--Weyl duality, every such endomorphism is an element of the Hecke algebra.

The Hecke mass element of the vortex \varrho is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \tau\bigl(L_{\alpha_\varrho}\bigr)
  \;\in\; H_n(R, q).

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces) induces an idempotent decomposition within H_n(R, q):

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  =
  \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta)
  +
  \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta),

where \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}} = \tau(\hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha})) encodes the base-level (descended) cycle and \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}} = \tau(L_{\alpha} - \hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha})) encodes the transient contributions at the blow-up centres.
